content:
alex: Heads-up — multiple multi-GPU jobs failing in us-west-2c with NCCL transport errors after last week's kernel/driver bump. Seen across pcluster-3*/rack-7.
maria: ugh, logs? NCCL errors or IB handshake?
alex: NCCL reports "Transport retry exceeded" and a bunch of runtime hangs. Sample: `NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed: 12` then hangs.
samir: Can you paste `ip link` / MTU + `ibv_devinfo` and ethtool stats from a failing host?
alex: attaching quick snippets: 
```
# ip link show ens5f0
5: ens5f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether b0:... brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# ibv_devinfo -v | head -n 6
hca_id: mlx5_0
        transport:                    InfiniBand (0)
        fw_ver:                       17.26.1020
# ethtool -S ens5f0 | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buf"
     rx_errors: 0
     tx_errors: 0
     rx_no_buf: 12
```
maria: MTU 9000 on host, that's expected. Any differences on the ToR/switch side?

alex: I checked with network team — switches set to 9216. But noticed these hosts are using VXLAN overlay for tenant isolation (we're using VXLAN/Geneve in a few racks).
vijay: VXLAN + RoCE is risky — offloads can do weird things. Which kernel/driver version after bump?

alex: Kernel 5.15.xxx + MLNX_OFED 5.0.1 (rolled last Wednesday).
samir: Can you run `ethtool -k ens5f0` and `tc -s qdisc show dev ens5f0`? Looking for GRO/LRO/tx offload state and drops in qdisc.
alex: results: 
```
ethtool -k ens5f0
     tx-checksumming: on
     rx-checksumming: on
     scatter-gather: on
     tcp-segmentation-offload: on
     generic-segmentation-offload: on
     tx-udp_tunnel-segmentation: on
     rx-udp_tunnel-port-remap: off

# tc
qdisc mq 0: dev ens5f0 root refcnt 2 bands 0 priomap ...
    backlogs:  handled 0  sent 0  dropped 34
```

vijay: dropped 34 at qdisc — not great. If VXLAN offloads are enabled, GSO/GRO/TSO may produce large tunneled frames that RoCE can't handle (RoCE requires L2/ETH behavior and small UDP payloads for encapsulated RDMA). We hit fragmentation/offload interaction.

infra-oncall: infra-oncall here — we have a known mlx5 bug where vxlan offload + TSO yields bad segmentation pre-OFED 5.1. Symptoms match: intermittent tx-side drops and ibv_post_send failures. There was an MLX vendor KB about disabling vxlan_offload on affected kernels.
maria: can we repro by disabling vxlan offload on one host?
samir: quick test patch: `ethtool -K ens5f0 tx-udp_tunnel-segmentation off` and `sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=...` and then restart a stuck job on same host.
alex: did that on pcluster-3a-17: `ethtool -K ens5f0 tx-udp_tunnel-segmentation off` -> restarted epoch job -> NCCL job completed 2 hours with no hangs. :tada:
vijay: nice — that strongly points to vxlan seg offload issue.

alex: rolling to another failing host now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: note: patch applied on pcluster-3a-17 by alex at 1769500342
samir: we should decide patch plan: either globally disable vxlan offload on affected fleets or upgrade MLNX_OFED/kernel to fixed version. Which is lower risk?

infra-oncall: short term: disable tx-udp_tunnel-segmentation on all hosts in VXLAN racks for now. Longer term: schedule MLNX_OFED + kernel upgrade to vendor-patched version (5.1+) and validate with stress harness.
maria: can we add a prom metric for `net_dev_dropped` per host and an alert if it spikes on RDMA racks?

vijay: also add a canary job hitting NCCL allreduce on a few nodes after driver upgrade. If the canary fails, automatically rollback driver via image fallback.
alex: I've started a playbook PR: `infra/playbooks/rdma/vxlan-offload-disable.yml` with target racks and an idempotent ethtool call + verification.
samir: please include a pre-check that MTU and switch config match; don't want accidental fragmentation.

alex: noted. Quick notes for postmortem: root cause — VXLAN/GSO (tx-udp_tunnel-segmentation) + MLX5 OFED regression causing improper segmentation of tunneled RDMA traffic -> qdisc drops -> ibv_post_send failures -> NCCL hangs. Fix applied: offload disabled; plan: vendor driver upgrade + canary.
maria: thanks. Add timeline to incident doc and tag networking + runtime teams.

infra-oncall: filing follow-up ticket: RDMA-4567, will track fleet rollout and vendor confirmation.
vijay: :thumbsup:

alex: will post summary to #incidents and schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow for rollout plan.
maria: thx everyone.
